title: [IELTS Trainer] - Museum floor plan changes
prompt: The plans below show the layout of the ground floor of a museum in 1990 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The floor plans illustrate the changes made to the ground floor layout of a museum between 1990 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the museum underwent significant reorganization to accommodate more visitor-oriented facilities. The most notable transformation was the replacement of the archaeology gallery with a café, gift shop expansion, and a children's interactive zone, while the core historical exhibition spaces remained largely intact.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the left side of the building, in 1990, there was a separate gift shop in the top left corner, adjacent to a natural history room below it. By 2010, the gift shop had been combined with a café to create a larger café and gift shop area. The natural history room remained in the same location, although a lift was added to its right. Meanwhile, the entrance area was extended to become wider, and the reception counter, which was originally positioned horizontally near the entrance, was repositioned at an angle by 2010.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the right side of the museum, in 1990, the archaeology gallery dominated this section, occupying a substantial rectangular space, while the local history room was situated in the bottom right corner. Twenty years later, the archaeology gallery had been entirely removed and replaced by three new areas: a children's interactive zone in the top right, a poster display area in the middle right, and an expanded local history room at the bottom. Finally, one of the most significant chage was the statue since it was relocated from the top left area in 1990 to a central position after two decades.
